Hi!

I am trying to build a project with R Shiny and am running into roadblocks all the time.

So far I have worked through the official Tutorial, looked through the examples and so on.

I wonder if there is any more extensive documentation out there, because I would really like to learn more about the different functions and party of Shiny so I can build on what (little) I know of R and how to convert an R graph into a Shiny App.

This path is not yet clear to me.

What I have so far is a data set with a row of years, and two rows with respective numbers of incidents in every year. I want to show two line graphs, both together and apart, and let the release years of to movies, each relevant to one of the line graphs show (or not).

If you have any pointers to more documentaion or things I should look at, that would be very welcome.

Best regards,

Ragni

messages.subject: Re: Running into Roadblocks - Is there more extensive documentation
parts:
Sorry for the delay, I have been on vacation for the past week.

There's no particular place the data would need to be stored; one common pattern is to put it in your app directory as a .csv file (or multiple CSV files). Then in your server.R file you can use the read.csv function with a relative path (e.g. if the file was "foo.csv" you would simply read.csv("foo.csv")), as the process's current directory is always set to the app directory when a Shiny application is run.

If you're not sure where in server.R you should call read.csv(), then take a look at the Scoping section of the tutorial.

If your application is not showing errors but also not showing a plot, these are two common reasons:
  1. When generating ggplot2 plots in renderPlot(), you need to explicitly call print(). So the above would become:
    print(ggplot(Molten, aes(x=time, y=value, colour = variable)) +geom_line())
  2. Make sure you're using a current version of your browser, and if it's not Chrome, Safari, Firefox, or IE10 then let us know what it is.
For showing one graph, the other, or both, consider using tabs. For showing the release years or not, that would just be a checkboxInput in your sidebar.

I hope that helps. If you need more detailed help, feel free to send a .zip archive of what you've currently got, either to me directly or to the list.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Running into Roadblocks - Is there more extensive documentation
parts:
Shiny Server doesn't implicitly read .RData files from inside the app directory. We've found this to be a common source of errors. However, I can see in your code that you're also explicitly defining RoseBella in server.R, so that isn't the problem.

The problem here is that in your ggplot aesthetics, you're including the dataframe:
  aes(y = RoseBella$Rosemary.Rosemary)
where only the column is needed:
  aes(y = Rosemary.Rosemary)

ggplot2 knows to evaluate the aes arguments in the context of the data argument you passed to ggplot(). I imagine you'll wonder, then, why it works when you test the code outside of Shiny. Well even though the latter code is "better", the former still ought to work, were it not for this bug in ggplot2.

Anyway, if you make the change above then you'll see everything start to work.
